turns.speaker: Helena Marsh
turns.text: The lease lets the tenant break on thirty-one March twenty thirty with six months' written notice.

turns.speaker: Oskar Lund
turns.text: Operations want to leave at the break date if the new warehouse is ready.

turns.speaker: Lena Ekdahl
turns.text: Finance has not yet modelled the cost of staying another five years.

turns.speaker: Oskar Lund
turns.text: We decide today to keep the break option open and not to waive it in any negotiation.

turns.speaker: Helena Marsh
turns.text: Then I will diarise the last date for serving notice and confirm it to you in writing next week.

turns.speaker: Lena Ekdahl
turns.text: The landlord says the roof leak is our responsibility.

turns.speaker: Helena Marsh
turns.text: Clause six point two puts the structure and roof on the landlord, so we disagree.

turns.speaker: Oskar Lund
turns.text: We agree to reject the landlord's demand and ask them to repair the roof.

turns.speaker: Lena Ekdahl
turns.text: I will collect the photographs and repair invoices by the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Oskar Lund
turns.text: It is unclear whether the insurer will cover the stock damaged by the leak.

turns.speaker: Helena Marsh
turns.text: I will write to the landlord about the roof once Lena sends me the photographs.

turns.speaker: Oskar Lund
turns.text: Let's meet again in a month to decide on the break.
